newsitem.title: UK: Skyepharma and Roche gain Swiss approval for drug.
newsitem.headline: Skyepharma and Roche gain Swiss approval for drug.

text.p: British drug group SkyePharma Plc said on Monday it had won regulatory approval in Switzerland for MADOPAR-DR, a controlled release formulation of Roche's treatment for Parkinson's disease.

To be launched in Switzerland this year, MADOPAR-DR is expected to offer important benefits in the treatment of Parkinson's disease, SkyePharma said. It is being jointly developed by a SkyePharma unit in partnership with Roche Pharma (Schweiz) AG.
MADOPAR-DR is the first product to receive marketing approval which uses "Binary" GEOMATRIX technology pioneered by SkyePharma's JAGO unit.
The technology allows two drugs to be delivered simultaneously from a single multi-layer tablet with different release profiles.
In the case of MADOPAR-DR, the tablet releases levodopa and benzerazide, a combination used in the management of Parkinson's.

JAGO will receive royalties on net sales and manufacture the product on behalf of Roche at its Muttenz (Basel) factory. It may ultimately begin manufacturing the product at its new plant near the French city of Lyon.
